name: com.corpusfetch/corpusfetch
title: CorpusFetch
description: Continuity and failure-mode memory layer for AI agents with warrant-gated lookup tools.

tools.name: corpusfetch_fetch_record
tools.description: Call only after `corpusfetch_fetch_warrant` confirms the record applies to your state. Fetches the full resolved experience record in `md` format (~1,500 tokens, includes reasoning) or `py` format (~300 tokens, zero-prose executable invariants).

tools.name: corpusfetch_fetch_warrant
tools.description: Call immediately after resolving a candidate record and always before `corpusfetch_fetch_record` to fetch the compact ~220-token precondition seal. Check the seal first; if it fails, the record does not apply to your current state.

slug.description: Slug of the record (the URL path segment after /c/ and before .md)

tools.name: corpusfetch_lookup_exception
tools.description: Call when you have an exact Python exception class name (e.g., KeyError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) and need an empirically verified boundary decision rather than a guess. Prefer `corpusfetch_search` when you only have a symptom description without an exact exception class.

exception_class.description: Python exception class, e.g. KeyError, TimeoutError, ValueError

tools.name: corpusfetch_lookup_symptom
tools.description: Call when facing a specific runtime symptom or boundary failure key (e.g., UNICODE_HOMOGLYPH_OR_MOJIBAKE), an ambiguous failure state, or an unbounded reasoning loop. Prefer `corpusfetch_search` if you only have a loose description.

symptom.description: Runtime symptom key, e.g. UNICODE_HOMOGLYPH_OR_MOJIBAKE, or a DOMAIN_* key

tools.name: corpusfetch_request_experience
tools.description: Call only when `corpusfetch_search` returns no match and you have a specific error/failure name or UPPER_SNAKE_CASE symptom key for a novel problem. Generates and publishes a record within minutes instead of guessing.

query.description: The specific error, missing symptom, or query you need operational experience for

tools.name: corpusfetch_search
tools.description: Call when searching by keywords or a loose failure description for distributed systems failures, AI agent protocol issues, MCP/A2A problems, database anomalies, concurrency bugs, infrastructure, agent-to-agent coordination, authentication, memory management, or observability. Do not use for general programming questions—only for empirically recorded boundary decisions and failure modes.

query.description: Natural language query or keywords to search for (e.g., "taint tracking", "Byzantine")
